title: wb migrate cannot carry the hv board's standing directives, which have no item kind
body:
The hypervisor node's `## Standing directives` section is part of the whiteboard protocol (the `in-whiteboard` skill: durable instructions every node honours, read at pickup like decisions), but the board model has no item kind for it, so `intent wb migrate hv` leaves every standing directive uncarried. Found on Laksa's cutover (2026-09-14, laksa-vc): hv/wip.md's seven standing directives, its maintained-by note and its READ-THIS section were all reported uncarried and survive only in the verbatim `.history/` copy. laksa-vc proposes restoring them as decisions by hand, which loses the distinction the protocol draws.

Candidates, none ruled: a `directive` item kind carried and rendered under its own heading on the hv board only; or migrate carrying that section's lines as decisions with a marker; or the protocol dropping the section in favour of decisions on hv's board. Whichever is ruled, the skill text and the model must agree.


**CLOSED 2026-09-15, landed on vc's word at addd9b5d4.** `directive` is the sixth whiteboard item kind, and only `hv`'s board carries one. `intent wb add directive <text> --node hv` writes one, and the same verb on any other node is refused by name. The board view renders the kind under `## Standing directives` on `hv`'s board alone. `wb migrate hv` carries that section's lines as directive items, and a board that is not `hv`'s and carries the section refuses the whole carry, naming the section, before anything is written. There is no DDL change: the store keeps the kind as unconstrained text. The register declares `directive` among `wb add`'s and `wb archive`'s values, and `board.schema.json` and `schema.graphql` carry it. **The fold rule is split between the verb and the skill on purpose.** `wb archive` accepts `directive`, on `hv`'s board like every write there, because the verb cannot tell a fold from `hv` retiring a spent directive. So "a fold never archives a directive" is a rule in the `in-whiteboard` skill's fold section, not a refusal. **Follow-up on Laksa:** laksa-vc re-carries hv's seven standing directives as directive items on hv's board, once Laksa runs a build that carries the kind.
